craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as rites relativized (not despised — relativized); two-means-two-results. Sanskrit-first: śamaka (DISPELLERS — rites' true result kept: heat dispelled, honored); cintā (CONTEMPLATING — the superior means is mental, kept); dhārā (STREAM-course — kept stream, not flood). Rows: 1 (‘bliss-stream in the mind’ closes — contemplation's result lands last, outshining by position), 9 (vow/giving/bathing/austerity — each rite named once, none adorned), 5 (didactic tread: concession L1, elevation L2). Close: ‘pours a bliss-stream in the mind’. Rupture: ‘But’ (rites turn to scripture — relativization hinged on one word). Rejected: ‘empty rites’ — killed: rites truly dispel heat; ‘flood’ — killed: dhārā courses; ‘holy writ’ for scripture — killed: śāstra kept plain (contemporary diction). Read aloud: TRU-ly, ŚAṄ-ka-ra — VOW, GIV-ing, BATH-ing, aus-TER-i-ty: they dis-PEL be-COM-ing's-HEAT … BUT con-TEM-plat-ing YOUR-scrip-ture … POURS a BLISS-stream IN the MIND.

lines: Truly, Śaṅkara — vow, giving, bathing, austerity: they dispel becoming’s heat.
But contemplating Your scripture as supreme nectar pours a bliss-stream in the mind.
l4.sanskrit_cite: śaṅkara satyam idam vratadānasnānatapaḥ bhavatāpavidāri tāvakaśāstra parāmṛtacintā cetasi nirvṛtidhārām syandati

reads_against.argmap: What do rites and scripture each accomplish? → Two means, two results: rites dispel heat, contemplation streams bliss.
c1_essence: Rites are relativized: vow, giving, bathing, austerity dispel becoming's heat — while scripture contemplated as nectar irrigates the mind with a bliss-stream.
Heat dispelled by rites; bliss streamed by contemplation. Two means, two results.
Rites are not despised; they are relativized, then the higher means offered.
